newsitem.title: UK: Gold sinks to new 3-1/4 year low.
newsitem.headline: Gold sinks to new 3-1/4 year low.

text.p: The price of gold descended to fresh 3-1/4 year lows on Friday, in a market that dealers said was wracked by widespread speculation about new central bank selling .
The overwhelmingly bearish market got a small but shortlived lift from news that Russia's state gold reserves were practically empty.
Bullion was fixed at $345.00 an ounce, the lowest since September 14, 1993, and down a dramatic $4.25 from Thursday afternoon's fixing.

Fresh rumours of central bank sales, just weeks after the Dutch central bank announced it had sold 300 tonnes from its reserves, injected a chill into the already nervous market, several dealers said.
"There is a very big sell order in the market and people suspect it is a central bank," one dealer said. "It's not confirmed but everyone is talking about it."
The market has been on edge watching gold plunge nearly seven percent since the start of 1997. Prices are also down some 17 percent since a blistering rally peaked at $417 almost exactly a year ago.
After the rally subsided, gold lost favour with investors in favour of booming stock and bond markets in recent months.

Fears that European central banks will dispose of some of their huge reserves, in order to raise money to meet budget criteria for membership in European Monetary Union, has also deepened the market's chill and sent prices tumbling in recent weeks.

"It's as bearish now as it was bullish a year ago. There is talk of central bank sales now as there was talk of a mystery buyer a year ago," said bullion analyst Andy Smith of Union Bank of Switzerland.

"If sentiment has a role in any market it's got the biggest role in the gold market. If the price goes up $5 today they'll be bullish. It's whipsawing around on its jagged way down, and sentiment is extremely fickle," he added.
After the fixing prices bounced up from early lows below $345 an ounce, then edged up another $0.65 following the potentially bullish news that Russia's gold reserves were virtually exhausted.

In the near term, technical analysts said, gold was likely to find historic support or perhaps even a bottom around $340, the low area of September 1993. But others have forecast declines to $325 an ounce, the lowest point from that year.
Platinum continued following gold's lead, tumbling some $3.00 from Thursday's highs to fix at $350.25 an ounce, the lowest since March 1993.
Consumer interest was expected to emerge around that level, but further losses towards $340 an ounce were not ruled out, some dealers said.
Silver meanwhile, was up eight cents at $4.96/$4.98 and continued to buck gold's downtrend in what dealers said was a play on the gold-silver ratio by U.S. investment funds.
"It became very clear yesterday, when gold fell and silver rose some eight cents, that hedge funds in New York were selling gold and buying silver," a dealer said.

On the upside silver is likely to encounter stiff resistance just above they key $5.00 an ounce level as profit taking emerges. But the downside is also well defended between $4.65 and $4.85. analysts said.
Palladium, which frequently ignores trends in the other precious metals, was little changed at $121.25/$122.25 an ounce.
